newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: ML&H says to seek deposit back from Manila.
newsitem.headline: ML&H says to seek deposit back from Manila.

text.p: Thai-Filipino consortium Manuela Land & Houses (ML&H) said it would seek a refund of its 100 million peso deposit after the Philippine government on Wednesday cancelled its winning bid for Camp John Hay.

"That's one of the options ...that is certainly one of the things we will go after, a return of the 100 million (pesos), ML&H Corp president Sulficio Tagud told Reuters when asked for a reaction after the government's announcement.
"The reputation of the company is at stake," Tagud added.

The government's Bases Conversion Development Authority (Basecon) said it had declared ML&H "in default" for failing to meet a deadline to sign a lease agreement for the development of Camp John Hay, a former U.S. army base in the northern hill resort of Baguio.
A Basecon statement said the project would instead be awarded to the second highest bidder, a group composed of Fil-Estate Land and local investment house Penta Capital Investment Corp.
"ML&H automatically forfeited its 100 million peso deposit," the Basecon statement said.
Tagud said ML&H had yet to receive an official notice from Basecon informing them of the cancellation of their bid.
ML&H bid 1.588 billion pesos to develop and operate Camp John Hay. Its bid was about four times higher than the next offer.
The ML&H consortium is formed by Philippine shopping mall owner Manuela Corp, which is not listed, and Thai property firm Land & Houses Plc.
The other members of the consortium are AB Capital and Investments Corp, Asia Pacific Planning and Evaluation Co Inc and First Asia Eagles Capital Corp.
ML&H refused to sign the lease, saying that only 121.77 hectares of land was available for development and not the 247 hectares mentioned in the bid documents.
